notes.meaning: The chapter opens with the three sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. These three men became the heads of the main branches of the tribe set apart for God's holy work. The writer gives a careful record of Levi's family because the priest's right to serve depended entirely on his family line.

Kohath's four sons are listed next: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. Kohath is singled out first among Levi's grandsons because the priestly family came through his line. His descendants were later assigned special duties caring for the most sacred objects in the worship of God.

Amram was the father of Aaron, Moses, and Miriam, the leaders God used to free Israel from Egypt. Aaron and his sons were chosen to serve as priests, offering sacrifices for the people. Nadab and Abihu died early under God's judgment for offering unauthorized fire, so the priesthood continued through Eleazar and Ithamar.

The line of the high priest is traced through Aaron's third son, Eleazar, and his son Phinehas down to Abishua. Phinehas was remembered for his bold zeal in turning God's anger away from Israel. Following Eleazar's line shows how God kept His promise to preserve this priestly family.

This list traces the line from Abishua through Bukki, Uzzi, Zerahiah, Meraioth, Amariah, and Ahitub. Little is recorded about these men, but their names demonstrate an unbroken family chain. During part of this era, the high priest's duties shifted over to Eli's family before returning to this branch.

Ahitub was the father of Zadok, who served faithfully as high priest under King David and King Solomon. Zadok stayed loyal to God's chosen king when others rebelled. Through him, the high priesthood returned firmly to the family line of Eleazar.

Ahimaaz was the father of Azariah, who fathered Johanan, the father of another Azariah. The writer notes that Azariah served as priest in the magnificent temple Solomon built in Jerusalem. He is commonly recognized as the brave priest who stood up to King Uzziah when the king tried to take over the priest's sacred duties.

The priestly lineage continued through another Azariah, Amariah, Ahitub, Zadok, and Shallum. Amariah served as high priest in the days of godly King Jehoshaphat. These names preserved the sacred family tree down through the history of the kings of Judah.

Shallum was the ancestor of Hilkiah, the high priest who discovered the lost Book of the Law during King Josiah's reforms. Hilkiah's grandson Seraiah served as the high priest when Jerusalem fell to the Babylonians. Seraiah was put to death by King Nebuchadnezzar, bringing that era of temple worship to a painful close.

Jehozadak was carried away into captivity in Babylon and never had the chance to serve as high priest in Jerusalem. The text makes clear that the Lord Himself sent the people into exile because of their sins, using Nebuchadnezzar as His tool. Ending this priestly list in captivity shows that the earthly priesthood could not bring final spiritual perfection.

The writer restates the three sons of Levi, using the spelling Gershom for the firstborn. The chapter now turns from the high priests to the Levites who served in other temple duties. It begins by listing Gershom's two sons, Libni and Shimei, who founded large family groups.

The sons of Kohath and Merari are repeated to complete the record of Levi's grandsons. Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. These names mark the official founding heads of the Levite clans that helped care for the house of the Lord.

This genealogy traces one branch of Gershom's family through Libni down to Jeatherai. Seven generations are recorded to preserve the heritage of this family group. These Levites had an honored place helping with worship, even though they were not priests.

This list follows a branch of Kohath's family from Amminadab down through Korah, Assir, and others to Shaul. Amminadab is another name for Kohath's son Izhar. Even though Korah died when he rebelled against Moses, God showed mercy by sparing his sons and keeping their line alive.

The line of Elkanah is traced through several generations to another man named Elkanah. This family tree leads straight to the father of the prophet Samuel. Even though Samuel's family lived in the territory of Ephraim, this record proves they belonged to the tribe of Levi by birth.
